xl:group-[:has(#right-rail-recirc-active)]/article:max-w-none"><article class="article-content max-md:[&_p]:text-lg" data-cy="article-content"><p class="wp-block-paragraph">Uber’s business model is one of the most AI-forward in Silicon Valley. AI decides your ride price, optimizes your route, among other predictive features. But even with these advanced features, an Uber executive is sounding the alarm on the rideshare company’s AI spending.</p><div class="not-prose empty:contents [:has(*[data-empty=true])]:hidden clear-both"><div id="related-video"><div class="flex flex-col gap-6"><div class="flex flex-col items-center gap-4"><span class="typography-level-3 font-graphik-compact font-semibold">Recommended Video</span><hr class="w-[150px] self-center border-t-4 stroke-red md:w-50"></div></div></div></div><div class="paywall-selector"></div><div class="paywall">



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">In a <a aria-label="Go to https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=y_mQ6xLcKyc" href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=y_mQ6xLcKyc">recent interview</a> on the <em>Rapid Response</em> podcast, Uber president and chief operating officer Andrew Macdonald said it’s hard to draw a connection between the company’s rising use of Claude Code and innovations meant to serve consumers.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">“That link is not there yet,” he said. “Maybe implicitly there’s more that is getting shipped, but it’s very hard to draw a line between one of those stats and ‘Okay now we’re actually producing like 25% more useful consumer features.’”</p><div class="not-prose empty:contents [:has(*[data-empty=true])]:hidden clear-both"><div class="min-h-[250px] xl:group-[:has(#rightRail):not(:has(.paywallActive))]/article:min-h-[280px] isolate z-body-popover [&>.contents]:contents flex items-center"><div class="w-full xl:group-[:has(#rightRail):not(:has(.paywallActive))]/article:flex xl:group-[:has(#rightRail):not(:has(.paywallActive))]/article:absolute xl:group-[:has(#rightRail):not(:has(.paywallActive))]/article:left-0 xl:group-[:has(#rightRail):not(:has(.paywallActive))]/article:right-0 xl:group-[:has(#rightRail):not(:has(.paywallActive))]/article:min-h-[280px] xl:group-[:has(#rightRail):not(:has(.paywallActive))]/article:bg-secondary xl:group-[:has(#rightRail):not(:has(.paywallActive))]/article:border-y-1 xl:group-[:has(#rightRail):not(:has(.paywallActive))]/article:stroke-secondary firstInstreamAdContainer"><div class="flex justify-center items-center w-full"><div class="absolute h-[1px] w-[1px] impression-element" data-cy="in-stream-0"></div><div class="text-center min-h-[250px] flex items-center"><div><div class="ad-slot-wrapper" id="fortunecom_incontent0"></div></div></div></div></div></div></div><div class="not-prose empty:contents [:has(*[data-empty=true])]:hidden clear-both"></div>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">The comments follow reports that the firm had already burnt through its entire 2026 AI coding tools budget in just four months after incentivizing employees to adopt the technology through an internal leaderboard ranking teams by total AI tool usage. It’s the latest development in a complex quandary arising in enterprise AI adoption: <a aria-label="Go to https://fortune.com/2026/05/22/microsoft-ai-cost-problem-tokens-agents/" href="https://fortune.com/2026/05/22/microsoft-ai-cost-problem-tokens-agents/">increasing AI use comes with higher costs</a>, even as per-unit AI pricing falls. </p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">“If you’re not actually able to draw a direct line to how [many] useful features and functionality you’re shipping to your users, that trade becomes harder to justify,” Macdonald said.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Uber isn’t the only company facing this issue. <a aria-label="Go to https://fortune.com/company/microsoft/" href="https://fortune.com/company/microsoft/" target="_blank">Microsoft</a> earlier this month reportedly began canceling most of its direct Claude Code licenses, according to <a aria-label="Go to https://www.theverge.com/tech/930447/microsoft-claude-code-discontinued-notepad" href="https://www.theverge.com/tech/930447/microsoft-claude-code-discontinued-notepad"><em>The Verge</em></a>, instead moving engineers toward using GitHub Copilot CLI. A number of other business leaders have walked back their initial bullish AI views. Duolingo CEO Luis von Ahn last year <a aria-label="Go to https://fortune.com/2025/05/24/duolingo-ai-first-employees-ceo-luis-von-ahn/" href="https://fortune.com/2025/05/24/duolingo-ai-first-employees-ceo-luis-von-ahn/">reversed</a> his outlook on AI, saying he doesn’t see the tech replacing the tasks his employees perform.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Uber didn’t immediately respond to <em>Fortune</em>’s request for comment.</p><div class="not-prose empty:contents [:has(*[data-empty=true])]:hidden clear-both"><div class="max-md:min-h-[250px] md:contents isolate z-body-popover [&>.contents]:contents flex items-center"><div data-empty="true"></div></div></div><div class="not-prose empty:contents [:has(*[data-empty=true])]:hidden clear-both"></div>



<h2 class="wp-block-heading"><strong>Can firms justify their AI spending?</strong></h2>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">In an earnings call earlier this month, Uber CEO Dara Khosrowshahi said about 10% of the company’s committed code is built by autonomous agents. Though he added that the firm’s AI use extends beyond its software engineers. </p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">“We’re seeing uptake of these tools, whether it’s our legal team or marketing team or developers,” he said. “We think it’s creating employees with superpowers.” </p><div class="not-prose empty:contents [:has(*[data-empty=true])]:hidden clear-both"><div class="max-md:contents md:min-h-[250px] isolate z-body-popover [&>.contents]:contents flex items-center"><div class="w-full xl:group-[:has(#rightRail):not(:has(.paywallActive))]/article:max-w-[745px] xl:group-[:has(#rightRail):not(:has(.paywallActive))]/article:overflow-x-hidden xl:group-[:has(#right-rail-recirc-active)]/article:max-w-none!"><div class="flex justify-center items-center w-full"><div class="absolute h-[1px] w-[1px] impression-element" data-cy="in-stream-1"></div><div class="text-center min-h-[250px] flex items-center"><div><div class="ad-slot-wrapper" id="fortunecom_incontent1"></div></div></div></div></div></div></div><div class="not-prose empty:contents [:has(*[data-empty=true])]:hidden clear-both"></div>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">But with more AI use comes higher costs. A recent study from research firm <a aria-label="Go to https://fortune.com/company/gartner/" href="https://fortune.com/company/gartner/" target="_blank">Gartner</a> found that by 2030, inference on highly sophisticated AI models will cost AI firms 90% less than 2025 costs. But the research also found cheaper tokens won’t translate to cheaper enterprise AI because agentic models require far more tokens per task than standard models, and because AI providers won’t fully pass through lower costs to consumers.</p><div class="not-prose empty:contents [:has(*[data-empty=true])]:hidden clear-both"><div class="nativo-wrapper min-h-[270px] md:min-h-[200px] sm:max-h-[570px] md:max-h-auto py-4 box-content"><div class="nativo-tout nativo-tout--in-content" data-cy="nativoTout"></div></div></div>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Some AI firms are shifting pricing plans to capture increased AI usage. Anthropic changed its pricing model, moving away from a flat fee to a usage-based model, meaning autonomous agents are now charged per token of compute use. In March, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman <a aria-label="Go to https://fortune.com/2026/03/12/sam-altman-ai-labor-capital-jobs-nobody-knows/" href="https://fortune.com/2026/03/12/sam-altman-ai-labor-capital-jobs-nobody-knows/">articulated</a> the industry’s broader direction during an interview. </p><div class="not-prose empty:contents [:has(*[data-empty=true])]:hidden clear-both"><div class="max-md:min-h-[250px] md:contents isolate z-body-popover [&>.contents]:contents flex items-center"><div data-empty="true"></div></div></div><div class="not-prose empty:contents [:has(*[data-empty=true])]:hidden clear-both"><div class="max-md:min-h-[404px] md:contents flex items-center"><div data-empty="true"></div></div></div>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">“We see a future where intelligence is a utility, like electricity or water, and people buy it from us on a meter,” he said.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">A separate Gartner study forecasts AI agent software spending will reach nearly $207 billion in 2026, up more than 139% from the $86.4 billion spent in 2025.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Uber spent 3.4% on research and development in 2025, a 9% increase from 2024. The company spent $951 million on research and development in the first quarter of 2026 alone, a nearly 17% increase from the same time a year ago. </p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Still, Uber isn’t shying away from technological innovation. Macdonald said the firm is going all in on autonomous driving, something he sees becoming the norm in under a couple decades.</p><div class="not-prose empty:contents [:has(*[data-empty=true])]:hidden clear-both"><div class="min-h-[250px] isolate z-body-popover [&>.contents]:contents flex items-center"><div class="w-full xl:group-[:has(#rightRail):not(:has(.paywallActive))]/article:max-w-[745px] xl:group-[:has(#rightRail):not(:has(.paywallActive))]/article:overflow-x-hidden xl:group-[:has(#right-rail-recirc-active)]/article:max-w-none!"><div class="flex justify-center items-center w-full"><div class="absolute h-[1px] w-[1px] impression-element" data-cy="in-stream-2"></div><div class="text-center min-h-[250px] flex items-center"><div><div class="ad-slot-wrapper" id="fortunecom_incontent2"></div></div></div></div></div></div></div><div class="not-prose empty:contents [:has(*[data-empty=true])]:hidden clear-both"><div class="min-h-[404px] flex items-center"><div class="flex justify-center items-center w-full [&_iframe]:ml-0" id="article-piano-template-plea-container"><div class="tp-container-inner" style="height: 391px; width: 745px;"><iframe id="offer_c740d28955713b1a5066-0" name="offer_c740d28955713b1a5066-0" scrolling="no" allowtransparency="true" allow="payment" allowfullscreen="true" src="https://vx.fortune.com/checkout/template/cacheableShow.html?aid=cfQj2fM3zj&templateId=OTRWPWWYYTDV&offerId=fakeOfferId&experienceId=EXU01L7HMKTJ&iframeId=offer_c740d28955713b1a5066-0&displayMode=inline&pianoIdUrl=https%3A%2F%2Fid.fortune.com%2Fid%2F&widget=template&url=https%3A%2F%2Ffortune.com%2F2026%2F05%2F26%2Fuber-coo-ai-spending-tokens-claude-code&isConsentManagerEnabled=false" frameborder="0" style="overflow: hidden; background-color: transparent; border: 0px; width: 745px; height: 391px;"></iframe></div></div></div></div>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">“I don’t think my daughters who are little kids today, I don’t think they will end up getting a driver’s license,” he said.</p>
